records.text: A spectral charger that attacks with a charge and follows the attack with a fear spell.
A spectral stallion that strikes with its hooves in combat.
A spectral stable hand, condemned to an endless routine of mucking out stables. Weariness colors its idle remarks, but it still warns intruders away.

Moroes, the Tower Steward, cautiously greets unannounced visitors. He gives changing reports about the Master's whereabouts, including study, rest, meetings with an apprentice, business upstairs, and a return from Stormwind.
Terestian Illhoof serves the Great One with fierce devotion. He conducts sacrifice rituals, offering victims' blood to anointed circles and speaking of his fealty and the Great One's approval.

Netherspite is a powerful creature encountered in Karazhan. It goes into a nether-fed rage and cries out in withdrawal as it opens gates to the Nether, marking it as a force tied to the tower’s nether activity.

Prince Malchezaar is the demon at the top of Karazhan whom Alturus identifies as a Burning Legion threat to the tower’s link with other worlds. He claims princely Eredar rank and command of legions, treating intruders as primitive playthings. He threatens to undo them and insists he will not concede defeat, grounding his defiance in his title.

A mechanical gallery attendant charged with protecting Karazhan’s Menagerie, the Curator restricts access to guests and enforces gallery rules. Its clipped, procedural warnings treat intruders as unauthorized visitors and threaten force for noncompliance.
Midnight is the undead mount who fights alongside Attumen in Karazhan. She answers his call and rushes to her master's aid, reflecting the close bond expressed by her encounter emotes.

Berthold is Karazhan's doorman, greeting travelers and offering assistance. His dialogue says bearers of a Karazhan key are honored guests of the Master; visitors can ask about Medivh and navigating the tower, or request transport to the Guardian's Library.
Calliard is Karazhan's Nightman, an attendant who greets guests of the Master and cautions them to watch their step inside the tower.
Hastings, titled the Caretaker, shows irritation with vermin and asks for help with an unspecified situation.
Coldmist Widow is a beast that fights with Frost Mist and Poison Bolt Volley.
A demon encountered in Karazhan, Shadowbeast answers combat with Howl of the Broken Hills.
A demon encountered in Karazhan, Dreadbeast attacks with Cleave.
A demonic Phase Hound found in Karazhan, it casts Phase Shift.

Koren is Karazhan's blacksmith, once paid by the Violet Eye to watch Medivh despite not being a member. He knows Keanna stayed in the guest chambers and was meant to keep her presence secret. He denies knowing the Violet Eye, yet remembers serving Medivh—or pretending to—and says all he can think about now is making horseshoes. He can be uncertain or guarded when approached about the Violet Eye, then returns to his work.
A spectral apprentice who challenges intruders, yet says they are lost when slain; their words pair hostility with confusion.
A phantom attendant who asks what is happening and where they are, then tries to master their fear. Their words convey disorientation and apprehension.
A spectral servant whose idle remark says they will never know the group is missing. When slain, they cry out and say they are finished.
A phantom valet who challenges anyone sneaking without an invitation and orders outsiders away. They also speak of fate turning against them and lament their death.
A phantom guest who fears it is their time to die and can no longer recall where they lived before.
A spectral retainer guards the master's dinner, angrily demanding that intruders leave. In death, the retainer sounds confused about its surroundings and afraid.
A spectral chef meets intruders with threats of chopping, gutting and carving them up, turning the language of food preparation into menace.
A ghostly baker threatens intruders with chopping, gutting and carving them up, using the grim vocabulary of preparing meat.
The ghostly steward resents the disturbance of the master's dinner and complains that a 200-year-old Pupellyverbos Port was wasted on the intruders.
The skeletal waiter answers requests with polished, deferential assurances, promising to check on matters right away and carry out orders.

A spectral sentry guarding Karazhan’s tower, this spirit raises the alarm when intruders appear and fights to stop them. Its brief cries treat the attackers as a threat to the tower; its combat role includes shooting at them.
A phantom guardsman defending Karazhan's tower, this spirit cries "To arms!" and "Protect the tower!" when intruders arrive, and can summon a phantom hound.

Bennett, Karazhan’s Sergeant at Arms, is responsible for training the tower’s men and women and keeping watch over the tower. He has little patience for idle conversation while occupied with those duties.

The Maiden of Virtue is a powerful, hostile presence in Karazhan who condemns intruders’ behavior and speaks of impurity, corruption, and cleansing. Her words frame her violence as punishment for moral failings, giving her an austere, judgmental character.

The Wanton Hostess is a flirtatious, sexually suggestive spirit in Karazhan. Her casual remarks describe paid encounters and partners’ behavior, while in a fight she turns possessive and threatening, inviting her target to play and insisting they will be hers.

A Night Mistress in Karazhan tells amused, blunt stories about a client who brought an imp along, charging extra and setting a five-second limit. Her remarks frame her as an experienced participant in the manor's adult entertainment.

The Concubine in Karazhan trades irreverent stories about clients for sharp flirtation: she invites people to play, boasts that they will be hers, and jokes about falling asleep during their encounters. She combines practiced, transactional confidence with a possessive edge.

A Spectral Patron in Karazhan recalls something of the show and says he will miss it, but turns hostile when others interfere. His few remarks suggest a revenant drawn to the manor's entertainment and protective of it.

The Ghostly Philanthropist in Karazhan sounds disoriented as memories return and wonders whether it is really over. When challenged, this spectral figure insists that the intruder was not invited and threatens to punish the disrespect.
The Skeletal Usher guards Karazhan's show, ordering intruders away and demanding to see their tickets. Its barks make clear that the performance is reserved for invited guests.

An unnamed spectral stagehand serves a master, tends to repeated set changes, and bars uninvited intruders. Its questions about release from duty and relief at work ending suggest it remains bound to its stagehand role.

An unnamed spectral performer is fiercely protective of the show, dismissing rivals as amateurs and insisting it must continue. Even in death, it worries about its name being spelled correctly on its tombstone, while its cold, dark surroundings unsettle it.
This unnamed haunting spirit bars visitors and threatens death to intruders. Its words suggest it longs to leave: it speaks of moving on and being free at last.
This trapped spirit bars visitors and threatens death to intruders. Its words suggest it longs to leave, speaking of moving on and being free at last.
An unnamed arcane watchman serves a master and threatens those who would steal from that master. It expects another to take its place and regards death as too merciful for its targets.
An Arcane Anomaly is a hostile magical being found in Karazhan. It casts Mana Shield when engaged.
Chaotic Sentience is a hostile elemental entity in Karazhan that lashes out with Unstable Magic.
A Mana Feeder is a hostile creature found in Karazhan.
A Syphoner is a hostile creature found in Karazhan; in combat, it drains mana from its opponent.

An Arcane Protector is a speaking guardian in Karazhan that calls intruders pillagers, desecrators, and thieves. When it dies, it warns that others will take its place, suggesting a continuing protective force.

The Shade of Aran identifies himself as Nielas Aran and refers to Medivh as his son, saying the son has gone mad. His combat words suggest he believes himself trapped in torment: he reacts with alarm, fights with fire and frost, and pleads for the nightmare to end. Shown Atiesh, he demands where it came from and asks if some "HE" sent the bearer.
The Spell Shade slips into phasing invisibility while out of combat.
The Sorcerous Shade attacks with Fireball Volley once combat begins.
The Magical Horror uses Power Distortion in combat.
At critical health, the Mana Warp triggers Warp Breach.
The Homunculus attacks with Firebolt in combat.
The Shadow Pillager claims its group was in the library first and means to keep its secrets. It calls intruders amateurs when they fall.

An ethereal thief guards the secrets of the tower library, warning intruders to turn back and claiming its knowledge for its own group. It treats outsiders as trespassers and attacks those who press on.

An ethereal spellfilcher claims its group was in the tower first and guards the library's secrets from outsiders. It warns away the uninitiated and regards the knowledge here as belonging to its own kind, meeting intruders with hostility.
A hostile fleshbeast fights with Gaping Maw and Infectious Poison.
A greater fleshbeast attacks with Gaping Maw.

Lord Ebonlocke is a Darkshire noble who resents being drawn into the nobles’ Karazhan gathering. He considers the party pointless, doubts the guests will reach Medivh, and says he would rather have stayed in Darkshire with his family.
Sebastian is Karazhan’s organist, proud of the instrument and honored to perform for the Master and his guests. He warmly invites visitors to join the audience for the coming show.

Barnes manages the stage and presents its plays with theatrical suspense, welcoming the audience before setting up each story. He also prepares visitors for a stage debut, making him both an emcee and a guide into the performance.

Wravien is a Violet Eye agent sent into Karazhan to help find Medivh’s journal. He becomes so absorbed in the library’s books that he loses track of the search and has trouble recalling what he was doing. He points the search onward to Gradav, who had also been looking for the book.

Gradav is a warlock researching in Karazhan’s Guardian’s Library. When asked about Medivh’s journal, he sends the search onward to Kamsis, explaining that leaving his own project would put his work at risk. He seems deeply absorbed in finding knowledge among the library’s books.

Kamsis is a conjurer and Violet Eye agent who was sent to Karazhan to look for Medivh’s journal. Absorbed in her scrolls, she has trouble keeping the search in mind. She recalls lending the journal to Aran, whom she identifies as Medivh’s father, and directs attention to a page that interests Archmage Alturus.

The Echo of Medivh guards his hall with a game of skill, requiring challengers to defeat him before they pass. He warns against complacency and lapses in concentration, insists on perfection and cheats when it suits him. Once beaten, he invites challengers to test their skills against one another.

Nightbane is an ancient, powerful creature encountered in battle. It mocks its opponents as vermin and insects, threatens to exterminate them, and alternates between attacking from the air and landing to crush them. Its awakening is announced from a distance.
Ythyar is a vendor who greets visitors by remarking that Karazhan is an odd place to find potential customers.
Skeletal Gryphon is a skeletal gryphon.
A human charger chess piece, described as standing proud and eager for battle.
A human cleric chess piece that watches you from the corner of its eye.
This chess likeness of King Llane is said to burn with the king's true wisdom and strength.
An orc necrolyte represented on the chess field, its fixed form marked by rippling dark magic.
An orc wolf chess piece, frozen in a snarl that gives it a fearsome presence on the field.
Warchief Blackhand is represented as a towering figure on the chess field.
Prince Tenris Mirkblood, the San'layn, savors blood and threatens to consume those he scents nearby. He greets approaching mortals as prey and promises them death.

place_records.text: You are in Karazhan, a tower reached through the Master's Cellar in Deadwind Pass. Moroes, the Tower Steward, greets unannounced visitors and gives changing reports of the Master's whereabouts. Prince Malchezaar, a demon at the top of the tower, is named by Archmage Alturus as a Burning Legion threat to its link with other worlds, and Nightbane, an ancient winged creature, attacks from the air and lands to crush those who come near. Phantoms, spectral patrons, mana feeders and syphoners fill its halls, and agents of the Violet Eye are still searching it for Medivh's journal.
